scenes.say: They say every seven years, you become a completely new person. You don't.
Your body does replace about three hundred and thirty billion cells every day.
But close to ninety percent of them are blood cells.
So does everything else run on a seven year clock?
Not even close. The lining of your gut is replaced every few days.
And your skeleton? About ten years.

visual.label: TO RENEW YOUR SKELETON
visual.note: most of it, about every 10 years (U.S. Surgeon General)

scenes.say: So what's actually happening inside your bones?
They're rebuilt from the inside, a little at a time, for your whole life.
